primerVape.title: The Complete Guide: How to Start Vaping and Choose Your Ideal Device

intro.paragraph1: Taking your first step into vaping can feel overwhelming given the sheer variety of formats, power levels, and e-liquid types out there. If you smoke and you're looking for a lower-risk alternative, public health bodies like the UK's National Health Service (NHS) note that vaping is significantly less harmful than smoking combustible tobacco. That said, it's not risk-free, and it's not meant for people who have never smoked.
intro.paragraph2: To make an informed switch, it helps to understand how devices are classified and which type of e-liquid goes with each one.

section1.title: Getting Started: Disposables and Swappable Pod Systems
section1.body: If you're just starting out, the best move is to go with a simple, lower-capacity option (400 to 1,500 puffs) at a moderate nicotine strength (2% or 3%), rather than jumping straight to the biggest device or 5% nicotine. This lets you get a feel for flavors, sensations, and satisfaction level without overspending.
section1.item1Text: These range from 400 all the way up to 70,000-puff models. Anything above 6,000 puffs typically includes a USB charging port so you can use up the full e-liquid capacity before tossing the device.
section1.item2Text: Devices like the Waka Creator or the Life Pod Eco 2 keep the same battery. Once the e-liquid runs out, you just swap in a new pre-filled pod — less waste, less hassle.

section2.title: Refillable (Open) Vapes: Nicotine Salts or Freebase?
section2.body: Once you're looking for more customization, refillable tank or open-pod devices come into play. Here, matching the device to the right e-liquid is essential:
section2.item1Text: Compact, low-power devices (10W to 20W) with high-resistance coils (0.8Ω to 1.2Ω). They use nicotine salts (20 mg/ml to 50 mg/ml), ideal for a tight mouth-to-lung draw, a smooth throat hit, and fast nicotine absorption with minimal vapor.
section2.item2Text: Larger devices with high power output (30W to 80W+) and low sub-ohm resistance (0.15Ω to 0.4Ω). They use traditional freebase nicotine at low concentrations (3 mg/ml or 6 mg/ml), producing big clouds with a direct lung draw.

section3.title: Why You Should Never Mix Up Your E-Liquids
section3.item1Label: Nicotine salts in a high-power mod:
section3.item1Text: Dangerous. Vaporizing 35 mg or 50 mg e-liquid at 50W delivers an excessive dose of nicotine in seconds, causing intense dizziness, nausea, and headaches.
section3.item2Text: Inefficient. Freebase e-liquids are thicker, so a small pod will burn through its coil fast due to poor wicking — and at just 3 mg or 6 mg of nicotine, you won't feel satisfied taking small, discreet puffs.

section4.title: Basic Device Care
section4.item1: Use standard chargers or a computer's USB port; avoid fast phone chargers, which can degrade the battery over time.
section4.item2: Keep devices away from direct heat sources or the inside of a car to prevent leaks.
section4.item3: Take slow, gentle puffs so the cotton has time to properly re-saturate between hits.

salesVsFreebase.intro: Picking the wrong e-liquid for your device isn't just a flavor issue — it can wreck the whole experience, or straight-up make you feel sick. Here's why, based on your device's ohm rating.

section1.title: What Are Nicotine Salts?
section1.body1: Chemically, it's the same nicotine found in freebase, but treated with an acid (usually benzoic acid) that lowers its pH. That change does two key things: it makes the throat hit dramatically smoother — even at high strengths, from 20mg to 50mg — and it gets nicotine into your system faster.
section1.body2: They work best in high-resistance devices (0.8Ω or more) at low power (10W to 20W) — the kind of setup that's typically a tight mouth-to-lung draw, which is exactly where salts perform best.

section2.title: What Is Freebase Nicotine?
section2.body1: This is nicotine in its traditional, untreated form. It has a higher (more alkaline) pH, which gives it that characteristic throat "kick" — enjoyable for some, harsh for others if the concentration is too high. That's why it's almost always sold at low strengths, between 3mg and 6mg: at higher concentrations, that kick gets uncomfortable fast.
section2.body2: It works best in low-resistance devices (0.5Ω or less) at high power (30W and up) — mods and sub-ohm setups built for a direct-to-lung draw and big clouds.

section3.title: Using Salt Nic in a High-Power (Sub-Ohm) Device
section3.body: Double trouble. First, salt nic usually comes in high concentrations (30-50mg) — at high power, each puff vaporizes way more e-liquid at once, so you end up inhaling far more nicotine than your body can comfortably handle. The result: dizziness, nausea, headaches, a racing heart. It's not random — it's a predictable chemical reaction.

section4.title: Using Freebase in a Small (Low-Power) Pod
section4.body: Here the problem runs the other way: since freebase usually comes in low concentrations (3-6mg) and a small pod already produces little vapor per puff, it's hard to feel satisfied — you'll end up taking way more puffs than you would with salts, without getting the same effect. On top of that, freebase tends to be thicker, and in a small coil without good airflow it can saturate the wick faster, leaving you with a burnt taste sooner than expected.

section5.title: The Simple Rule
section5.item1: Is your device rated 0.8Ω or higher? → Nicotine salts.
section5.item2: Is your device rated 0.5Ω or lower? → Freebase.
section5.item3: Closed pod system with no wattage adjustment? → Nicotine salts.
section5.item4: Open mod or tank with wattage control? → Freebase.
